#en: The Well is where routes are born and buried, where overworked clerks and forgotten terminals quietly decide which lives get a clean corridor and which ships vanish into a line item, so it is the only place she could twist the knife. Here, beneath the shining tiers of New Atlantis, Luna has spliced her private lattice into the transit grid, feeding on the same power and data that once made her indispensable to LIST. From this tangle of metal walkways and maintenance cubbies she is preparing to loose years of doctored charts and erased pings into every office that ever signed off on a convenient grav-drive failure, ready to redraw the politics of safe lanes in a single broadcast. Coincidences piled up to bring you to this junction: a gutted GalBank escort with route logs that did not match its manifest, an ambush in an asteroid field triggered the moment you touched a beacon carrying her signature checksum, patterns in traffic that stopped looking like noise and started to look like intent.
zh: 深井区，是航线诞生与埋葬之处；在那里，超负荷的文书与被遗忘的终端悄悄决定哪些人能得到干净的走廊、哪些船变成一行条目，所以这是她唯一能下刀的地方。在这里、在新亚特兰蒂斯城闪亮层级之下，露娜已把她的私人网格接进运输网，以那套曾让她对独立盟不可或缺的同样电力与数据为食。在这片由金属步道与维护隔间构成的乱麻里，她正准备把多年被做手脚的星图与被抹除的脉冲倾泻进每一个曾签批过"方便的引力引擎故障"的办公室，准备以一次广播重画安全航道的政治。巧合层层堆叠，把你带到这个枢纽：一具被掏空的盖尔银行护航船，航线日志与舱单不符；一场在你刚碰到一枚带着她签名校验和信标的瞬间触发的小行星带伏击；以及那些不再像噪声、而开始像意图的交通模式。

#en: If her work ever had a heartbeat, it was down here, where the queues knot around the LIST office and every name on a waiting slate is another pressure point she learned to twist. Buried in this tangle of ducts and drip stained bulkheads lie the silent tallies of who was moved forward, who was stalled, and who vanished into off grid promises; only here do the numbers line up with the faces that paid for them. The samples taken from these depths carry the faint, cumulative imprint of every quiet exception she pushed through, every application diverted to nowhere, the kind of subtle trace that can be followed back along the path she thought erased. So far the trail runs from a dead end contact in the back country to a sealed lab on a nameless world, to a nervous broker in Neon and a derelict survey ship with half a jump plan, and each step has confirmed the same pattern a hidden network of settlements threaded through the gaps in official records, all drawn to a point she once called Hearthline.
zh: 若说她的工作曾有过心跳，那就是在这下面——独立盟办公室周围人群打结、候补名册上每个名字都是她学会扭动的一个压力点。埋在这片导管与滴水舱壁的乱麻里的，是"谁被提前、谁被拖延、谁消失在账外承诺里"的无声清点；只有在这里，数字才与为之付钱的面孔对得上。从这些深处取出的样本，携带她推过的每一次安静例外的微弱累积印记，每一份被改道到虚空的申请——那种能沿着她以为已抹掉的路径回溯的微妙痕迹。目前为止，线索从乡间一名死掉联系人，到一颗无名世界上密封的实验室，再到霓虹城一名紧张的掮客与一艘只带着半份跃迁计划的弃置勘探船，每一步都证实同样的模式：一张藏在官方记录缝隙里的隐藏定居点网络，全都绘向一个她一度称作"炉线"的点。

#en: The old barracks sit half-swallowed by dust and silence, a place built to train soldiers how to kill and then abandoned when the war moved on without them; if any records survived the sanitizing, they would cling to a place like this, layered under drill routines and casualty tallies no one officially kept. Wayward Taskforce holding this ground tells you enough about what is hidden here, ex-operatives guarding a past they have all agreed never to have seen, stepping around scorch marks and nameplates as if they were just flaws in the concrete. Somewhere in these dead halls the trajectories that keep guiding ships into graveyards will be written down, if only in corrupted logs or forgotten briefing slates. So far the trail has been a lonely data scrap on a backwater world, a silent relay full of mismatched timestamps, and a gutted garrison with beacon code that did not match the wrecks outside, all pointing toward someone who knows exactly which details everyone else has chosen not to remember.
zh: 那座旧营房半被尘土与沉默吞没，一座为训练士兵如何杀戮而建、随后在战争把他们抛下继续前行时被弃置的设施；若有任何记录在清理中存活，它会黏在这样的地方，层层压在进行演练与没人正式保留的伤亡统计之下。任性特遣队据守这片地面，已足够说明这里藏着什么：一群前特工守着一段他们都同意"从未见过"的过去，绕着灼痕与铭牌走，仿佛它们只是混凝土上的瑕疵。在这些死掉的大厅里某处，那些不断把船只引向墓地的轨迹会被写下来——哪怕只在损坏的日志或被遗忘的简报数据板里。目前为止，这条线索是一穷乡世界上一块孤独的数据碎片、一座塞满对不上时戳的沉默中继，以及一座信标代码与外面残骸不符的被掏空驻军，全都指向某个确切知道"其他所有人选择不记得哪些细节"的人。

#en: This forgotten freight yard is a dead space in every registry, a place where cargo goes to be lost and paperwork goes to die. That makes it perfect for work no one wants to admit exists; perfect for a final adjustment to a grav system no inspector will ever audit, and for a saboteur who needs shielding from eyes in New Atlantis and Akila alike. Here the containers are stacked like tombstones, humming with old power, ready to amplify whatever she has wired into the conduits. If Vector completes what she is calibrating in this rusted maze, the next "accident" will not be local to some unlucky hauler, it will echo along whole trade lanes before anyone can respond. The UC and Deimos hoped the incidents would blur into background noise, that the Cheyenne files and the first vented testbed would dissolve into rumor, but scattered engineers, a LIST foreman, and a few nervous GalBank clerks kept the pattern alive long enough for the trail of shards, ghost code, and vanished consultants to point straight here.
zh: 这座被遗忘的货运场在每个登记册里都是死空间，货物来此失踪、文书来此死去。这让它成了"没人愿意承认存在的工作"的完美地点：一次任何检查员都不会审计的引力系统最终调整，以及一名需要躲开新亚特兰蒂斯城与阿基拉城眼线的破坏者。在这里，那些货柜像墓碑一样堆着，带着旧电力嗡鸣，随时放大她接进导管的任何东西。若"向量"完成她在这座锈蚀迷宫里校准的东西，下一场"意外"就不会只局限于某艘倒霉货船，它会在任何人能响应之前沿整条整条贸易航道回响。联殖与火卫二本希望那些事件模糊成背景噪声，希望夏延星文件与第一座被排空的试验台溶解成传闻，可零散的工程师、一名独立盟工头，以及几名紧张的盖尔银行文书，让这个模式活到足够久——久到由碎片、幽灵代码与消失顾问构成的线索直指这里。

#en: Gagarin Landing has always been a waystation, never a destination, which is why people talk too freely here and think nothing lingers longer than the dust from old mech yards. That makes its loading rings and backline clinics the perfect catch-basin for stories no one bothered to write down, the place where her name is never spoken but her habits are. Dockhands remember a certain soft accent, customs techs recall tiny gaps in sensor sweeps, and someone always knows a ship that was logged two minutes before or after it really arrived. All those slips and shrugs left small bends in the paperwork, faint grooves in memory, guiding certain crates and certain people along the same quiet channels until they ended up far from where the manifests said they should be. So far the trail is this: a discarded slate on an empty rock, a clinic's scrubbed patient list, and now a port where gossip, altered timestamps, and half-forgotten favors all point toward the same invisible courier shaping routes from the shadows.
zh: 加加林着陆点一向是中转站、从不是目的地，所以这里的人说话太随意，以为没有任何东西比旧机甲场的尘土留得更久。这让它的装货环与后方诊所成了"没人费心写下来之故事"的完美接水盆：她名字从不被提起、她的习性却在此地的地方。码头工记得某种柔和的口音，海关技师回忆起传感器扫描里的微小空隙，而总有人知道某艘船的被记录时间是早于还是晚于它真正抵达两分钟。所有那些口误与耸肩，都在文书里留下小小的弯折、在记忆里留下浅浅的沟槽，把某些货箱与某些人沿同样的安静渠道引去，直到他们最终落在舱单所说位置很远的地方。目前为止，这条线索是这样的：一空岩石上一块被丢弃的数据板、一份诊所被擦净的病人名单，如今又是一座闲话、被改动的时戳与半被遗忘的人情全都指向同一名从阴影里塑造航线的隐形信使的港市。

#en: The UC warship WK-9192 drifts in the dark like a monument to routine gone wrong, its hull marked by skirmishes everyone thought were already accounted for in the logs. This is where patrol routes, emergency deployments, and interdiction patterns were written and rewritten until the crew stopped questioning the math and simply trusted the console glow. Somewhere in that quiet confidence, her hand slipped in, bending familiar scripts into unseen corridors while officers signed off without a second glance. To understand how she has been hiding fleets in plain sight, the ship that trusted her calculations is the only place the pattern can be read clean. So far the trail runs from a nervous smuggler contact who swore their runs arrived early without burning extra fuel, to route discrepancies buried in customs reports, all of it pointing to one truth: someone with system-level access has been nudging traffic just far enough off expected vectors that no one noticed until ships started vanishing between lanes.
zh: 那艘联殖军舰"WK-9192"像一座"例行公事出了岔"的纪念碑般漂在黑暗中，船壳上留着所有人都以为早已计入日志的冲突痕迹。这里正是巡逻航线、应急部署与阻截模式被写下又被改写到船员不再质疑那套数学、只信任控制台辉光的地方。在那份安静的笃定里某处，她的手溜了进来，把熟悉的脚本掰成看不见的走廊，而军官们不假思索地签了字。要弄懂她一直在如何把舰队藏在明面上，这艘信任她计算的船，是唯一能干净读出那个模式的地方。目前为止，线索从一名发誓自己的航次没多烧燃料却提前抵达的紧张走私者线人，延伸到海关报告里被埋的航线差异，全都指向一个真相：某个拥有系统级权限的人一直在把交通推得刚够偏离预期向量，以至于没人注意到——直到船只开始在航道之间消失。

#en: The dead arrays of the deserted UC listening post still sweep the stars in slow, meaningless arcs, a relic that once heard every whisper along this stretch of space and then, somehow, missed the one that mattered most. Here, buried in half-scrubbed logs and obsolete grav telemetry, Starline could work unobserved, splicing his ghost corridors straight through the gaps in official attention. UC abandoned the place; he turned its quiet into a launchpad, feeding routes to captains while he watched which ships came back and which fell silent. You arrive as the last cycle completes, just as he moves to erase the final proof that his patterns ever ran through UC ears at all.  \n\nWe started with a stray dataslate in the back end of nowhere, then a buried analyst pod that hinted at doctored navigation reports, and finally a rigged beacon in high orbit broadcasting impossible jump solutions. Every step pointed to the same hand, the same spiral in the numbers, hiding in the blind spots everyone else chose not to see.
zh: 那座废弃联殖听音哨死掉的阵列仍以缓慢而无意义的弧线扫过群星，一件遗物——它曾听见这片太空沿线的每一句低语，然后不知怎地错过了最重要的那一句。在这里、埋在半擦除的日志与过时的引力遥测中，"星线"能不受观察地工作，把他的幽灵走廊直接接进官方注意力的空隙。联殖放弃了这地方；他把它的安静变成发射台，向船长们喂航线，同时观察哪些船回来、哪些陷入沉默。你在最后一个周期完成时抵达，正好在他动手抹掉"他的模式曾穿过联殖耳朵"的最后证据之时。  \n\n我们从天涯之外一块散落数据板开始，然后是一座暗示导航报告被动过手脚的被埋分析舱，最后是轨道上一座广播着不可能跃迁解的被动过手脚信标。每一步都指向同一只手、数字里同一个螺旋，藏在别人选择不去看的盲点里。

#en:
This empty relay sits on the rim of real traffic, where civilian ships fall off the charts and only maintenance drones were ever meant to listen.  
Its dishes still drink in background noise from the lanes, and that noise is the one thing Vector cannot fully scrub; every falsified route, every doctored misjump leaves a faint echo in its buffers.  
He has come here to collapse the pattern, purge the last record tying his algorithms to the wrecks scattered through Kessler's Veil and the test yards near Protectorate Systems.  
If he succeeds, the accidents become ghost stories, forever blamed on bad luck and faulty hardware no one can disprove.  
The trail to this place was stitched from half-heard bar talk in the hinterlands, a corrupted slate found where the first hint surfaced, garbled transponder logs pulled off a drifting hull, then contraband manifests pried from a frightened broker on that moonside module; no one ever had the full story, just fragments traded between people who learned to talk quietly.
zh:
这座空中继坐落在真实交通的边缘，民用船只在此脱离星图，只有维护无人机本该在此聆听。  
它的天线盘仍在啜饮航道传来的背景噪声，而那种噪声是"向量"唯一无法完全擦除的东西；每一条被伪造的航线、每一次被做手脚的错跳，都会在它的缓冲区里留下一道淡淡回声。  
他来这里是为了坍缩这个模式，清除"他的算法与散落在凯斯勒之幕及保护国系统附近试验场里的残骸有关"的最后记录。  
若他成功，那些事故就会变成鬼故事，永远被归咎于坏运气与无人能推翻的故障硬件。  
通往此地的线索，是由边境半听来的酒吧闲谈、一块在第一处线索浮现之地找到的损坏数据板、从一具漂移船壳上拉出的乱码应答器日志，以及从那座卫星侧舱室一名受惊掮客那里撬出的违禁舱单缝成的；没人拥有完整故事，只有在学会低声说话的人之间交易的碎片。

#en: Down here, beneath the neon sheen and corporate gloss, the conduits run like exposed nerves, every junction tagged, rerouted, and quietly stolen from. This is where maintenance logs are falsified, power siphons are normalized, and a single mislabeled junction can divert half a city's traffic without anyone topside noticing. That same complacency makes this spine the only place a former inspector could sketch safe corridors through the chaos, turning forgotten service tunnels and unregistered airlocks into a private transit map no security sweep will ever catch. A minor oversight in access control became a habit, then a custom, and now an invisible highway that only one saboteur truly understands. The trail so far began with a stray slate at a dead outpost and a cargo yard humming with unexplained drive faults; together they painted the outline of someone who knows every shortcut, prefers to work in the blind spots, and has been using abandoned infrastructure as waypoints between ruined ships and redacted reports.
zh: 在这下面、在霓虹光泽与公司亮面之下，那些导管像裸露的神经一样延伸，每个接点都被标记、被改道、被悄悄偷接。这里正是维护日志被伪造、电力虹吸被正常化，以及一个标签错误的接点就能改道半座城市交通而楼上无人察觉的地方。同样的自满让这道脊骨成了唯一能让一名前检查员在混乱中勾出安全走廊的地方，把被遗忘的服务隧道与未登记气闸变成一张任何安保扫描都抓不到的私人运输图。门禁控制里的一处小小疏忽变成了习惯，然后是惯例，如今成了一条只有一名破坏者真正理解的隐形高速公路。到目前为止，这条线索始于一死掉前哨上一块散落数据板与一片嗡鸣着无法解释的引擎故障的货运场区；合在一起，它们画出了某个"熟悉每一条近路、偏爱在盲点里工作、并一直把废弃基础设施当作废墟船只与涂黑报告之间航点"之人的轮廓。

#en: Only up on the rooftops can you hear Neon without the walls lying for it. The hum of grav pads and private shuttles passing just low enough to skim the Span is where contracts change hands, off the record, passed between executives who do not want their own systems seeing the numbers. Whatever was logged about Vector and his routes was never meant to sit in a clean office downstairs; it lives up here, tucked into side-channel traffic and rooftop relays that only the desperate and the crooked bother to touch. Word is, a smuggler bragged in a corner booth that their miracle escape corridor came from someone who talks in coordinates instead of names, and a nervous clerk mentioned forged permits that always pointed one jump beyond the usual lanes. Out in the hinterlands, a LIST camp swore a clipped voice walked them past a storm, and a drifting cutter near UC space carried logs stamped with a familiar sigil. Taken alone, each story is just bar talk. Lined up against the skyline, they all start whispering the same direction.
zh: 只有在屋顶上，你才能听见没有墙壁替它说谎的霓虹城。引力停机坪与私人穿梭机的嗡鸣低得刚好掠过桥架，那里正是合同在账外转手的地方，在那些不愿让自己的系统看见数字的高管之间传递。凡是关于"向量"及其航线的记录，从来就注定不会待在楼下一间干净的办公室里；它活在这里，藏在侧信道交通与屋顶中继里——只有走投无路者和歪门邪道者才会费心去碰。据说，一名走私者在角落卡座里吹嘘他们那条奇迹逃生走廊来自某个"用坐标而非名字说话"的人；一名紧张的文书提到总是指向"常规航道之外一次跃迁"的伪造许可。在边境，一支独立盟营地发誓有个简短的声音带他们走过了风暴；而在联殖太空附近一艘漂着的切割船，带着盖着熟悉印记的日志。单看，每个故事都只是酒吧闲谈。与天际线排在一起，它们都开始低语同一方向。

#en: The abandoned garrison sits at the edge of nowhere, its sirens long silenced, its walls thick with old militia dust and newer scorch marks that do not match any logged engagement. Whatever was dragged into its bunkers was meant to be buried under Freestar jurisdiction and forgotten, far from UC eyes and the ships Rivet likes to cut open. The Stray Rust Syndicate were hired to stand watch on something they only half understood, then bled away as the pay dried up and the rumors sharpened, leaving hardened sentries guarding a secret none of them could name. If this place is left intact, the pattern Rivet has been tracing between wrecks, stolen drives, and vanished convoys will find another outpost to infect. So far, the trail runs like this: a stray slate in deep space whispering about a shipbreaker with too many aliases, soil-stained scrap on a quiet farm stamped with Deimos marks, and now a deserted Freestar site where Syndicate guns loiter over tech that hums in the same wrong frequency as the anomaly pinned in UC archives.
zh: 那座废弃驻军坐落在天涯之外，警报早已沉默，墙壁厚积着旧民兵的尘土与更新、且与任何记录过的交火都不符的灼痕。凡是被拖进它掩体的东西，本都打算埋在自由星系联盟管辖下被遗忘，远离联殖的眼睛与"铆钉"喜欢切开的船。"游荡锈迹辛迪加"受雇看守一件他们只懂一半的东西，随后在薪酬枯竭、传闻变尖锐时渐次流失，只留下硬派哨兵守着一个没人说得出名字的秘密。若这地方被任其完好，"铆钉"一直在残骸、被偷引擎与失踪车队之间追查的模式就会找到下一个前哨去感染。目前为止，线索是这样：深空中一块散落数据板低语着一个绰号太多的拆船工、一座安静农场上带着火卫二标记的沾土废料，如今又是一处废弃自由星系联盟场址——辛迪加的枪口在那些以同样错误频率嗡鸣的技术上方闲晃，与联殖档案里钉住的异常一样。

#en: The Helium-3 plant is the last place she can work unseen, its automated rigs and sealed conduits perfect camouflage for someone who lives between manifest lines and maintenance schedules. Every pipe is a route, every pressure chamber another room where a mind can be tuned and a witness made to forget why they came here. Quietline needs these reactors to power and mask the neuroamps she has folded into the plant's control lattice, one final attempt to cut herself free of every record and every debt before UC, Freestar, or worse can close in. If she finishes rewriting the staff and the logs, she walks away as a ghost and the station becomes another blind spot in the Settled Systems, its crew loyal to a woman they cannot name. All we know for certain is this: a stray dataslate in the dark, half-scrubbed signatures around a backline clinic, and the altered testimony of a raider and a farmstead led from a quiet rock, through Gagarin's alleys and a hard-bitten refuge, to a courier whose trail never quite lines up with the reports.
zh: 氦-3 工厂是她唯一能不被看见地工作的地方，它的自动化设备与密封导管对某个活在舱单行间与维护日程之间的人来说是完美的伪装。每根管道都是一条航线，每个压力舱都是又一个房间，心智可以在那里被调校，证人可以在那里被弄得忘记自己为何而来。"静默线"需要这些反应堆来驱动并掩盖她折进工厂控制网格的神经增幅器，这是她在联殖、自由星系联盟或更糟的东西合围之前，切断自己与每一份记录、每一笔债务联系的最后一搏。若她完成对员工与日志的改写，她就会像幽灵一样走开，而这座星际站成为定居星系里又一个盲点，它的船员效忠于一个说不出名字的女人。我们唯一确定的是这些：漆黑中一块散落数据板、后方诊所周围半擦除的签名，以及一名掠夺者与一座农庄被改动的证词——它们从一块安静岩石，穿过加加林星的小巷与一处饱经风霜的避难所，引到一艘痕迹总与报告对不太上的信使船。

#en: Down here, where the grid hums overhead and leaking pipes keep their own slow time, this is the only place her routes would be written down honestly. Customs offices and starport kiosks deal in official lanes; the real paths run underfoot, traded between haulers, chem runners, and anyone desperate enough to risk a shortcut that does not exist on any map. Somewhere among these rusted bulkheads is the pattern of ships she has bent to her purposes, the off-hour departures and unscheduled dockings that only a courier from this city would trust. Every dockhand has a different version of how she moves and who she serves, the tale shifting a little with each retelling, like fear and superstition sand down the details no one wants to own. So far the trail runs like this: a discarded slate on a dead rock, scrambled logs in a back-room clinic near Gagarin, a rattled runner who remembers a soft accent and the wrong sigil on the right crate, all pointing toward the same invisible corridors she has been carving through the Settled Systems.
zh: 在这下面、在网格头顶嗡鸣、渗漏管道以自己缓慢节奏计时之处，这是唯一会如实写下她航线的地方。海关办公室与太空港小摊做的是官方航道；真正的路径在脚下流动，在货船船员、药剂跑腿，以及任何绝望到愿意冒一条任何星图上都不存在的近路风险的人之间交易。在这些锈蚀舱壁之间某处，是她掰向自己目的的船只的模式，是只有来自这座城市的信使才会信任的错峰离港与未排期停靠。每个码头工对"她如何行动、效忠于谁"都有不同版本，故事随着每次重述稍作偏移，仿佛恐惧与迷信把没人愿意认领的细节一点点磨掉。目前为止，线索是这样的：死岩石上一块被丢弃的数据板、加加林星附近某间后室诊所里被搅乱的日志、一名记得柔和口音与"正确货箱上错误印记"的心有余悸的跑腿，全都指向她一直在定居星系里凿出的同一些看不见的走廊。

#en: Out on the edge of the lane, the wreckage hangs in a slow tumble, its hull etched with scorch marks that do not quite match any honest misjump or weapons test. This is where stories diverge: freighter crews mutter about a ship that appeared sideways to its own trajectory, then sheared away like glass under a bad grav surge, while more sober traffic controllers dismiss it as panicked testimony and faulty sensors. The metal does not lie, though; the scoring and twisted struts sketch the kind of impossible turn only a pilot obsessed with shaving reality thin would attempt, and whoever was flying left just enough of their signature burned into the plating to trace the direction they were trying to escape in. So far, everything I have seen fits the same crooked outline: a forgotten rock with a half-wiped slate, beacons reporting ships where no flight plan put them, Neon's lower levels hiding power cuts nobody wants to log, and now this broken shell, floating exactly where all those rumors about ghost jumps insist something went wrong.
zh: 在航道边缘，那具残骸以缓慢翻滚悬着，船壳上刻着与任何诚实的错跳或武器测试都不太吻合的灼痕。这里正是故事分岔之处：货船船员嘟囔着一艘"相对自身轨迹侧着出现、随后在糟糕引力浪涌下像玻璃一样崩开"的船，而更冷静的交管员则把它当作惊慌的证词与故障传感器打发。可金属不会说谎；那些刮痕与扭曲的支柱，勾画出一种只有痴迷于把现实削薄的飞行员才会尝试的不可能转向，而驾驶者留在钢板上、足以追溯他们试图逃离方向的签名。目前为止，我见过的一切都契合同一道歪斜轮廓：一块带着半擦除数据板的被遗忘岩石、报告着"飞行计划中并不存在的船只"的信标、霓虹城下层隐藏着没人愿意记录的断电，以及如今这具破碎外壳——它就漂在所有那些关于幽灵跃迁的传闻坚称"出了问题时"的确切位置。

#en: Gagarin Landing looks the same on approach, all rusted gantries and tired floodlights, but the real work here has always been hidden in rote paperwork and unremarkable cargo runs. This is where freighters drift in from every direction, where manifests get adjusted, fees waived, and traffic patterns nudged a few degrees at a time without anyone raising their voice. If someone wanted to bend the lanes around a single pilot, to make their comings and goings disappear into a new normal, it would start in the ledgers and schedules no one reads twice. Only by pulling those quiet changes apart here can you see which ships began arriving early, which routes inexplicably rerouted around the same patch of sky, and how a forgotten station suddenly became a waypoint in everything from grain hauls to scrap deliveries. So far the trail runs from a ghost signal at an old listening post to buried scans in a relay bunker, each step showing the same unmarked ship cutting through restricted air while the official charts insist nothing unusual ever happened.
zh: 加加林着陆点从进近方向看依旧是老样子，满是锈蚀龙门架与疲惫泛光灯，可这里真正的活计一向藏在刻板的文书与不起眼的货运里。这是货船从各个方向漂来的地方，是舱单被调整、费用被免除、交通模式被一次几度地推动而没人抬高嗓门的地方。若有人想围绕一名飞行员掰弯航道、让他们的来去消失进一种新的常态，它就会始于那些没人读两遍的账册与日程。只有在这里把这些安静的改动拆开，你才能看出哪些船开始提前抵达、哪些航线莫名其妙地绕开同一片天空，以及一座被遗忘的星际站如何突然变成从谷物运输到废料交付的一切航次中的中转点。目前为止，线索从旧听音哨的一道幽灵信号，延伸到中继掩体里被埋的扫描，每一步都显示同一艘未标记的船切过受限天空，而官方星图坚称从未发生任何异常。

#en: It had to end at the edge of a city that lives on exhausted rock and old war ghosts, where ship lanes pinch low over the dust and every vector in and out passes through the same narrow sky. Out here, there is no crowd to vanish into, no storm corridor to ride; the only cover is the heat shimmer off Cydonia's scarred outskirts and the static whisper of overworked traffic beacons that Vector has tuned one too many times. He chose this place because its patterns are familiar, because a dozen minor route edits and quiet favors have slowly braided into a single escape line he thinks only he can see. Breaking that line here stops his last attempt to fold the map around himself before corporate cleaners or desperate smugglers turn his tricks into something far worse. So far the trail has run from a forgotten dataslate on a backworld, through a drifting Trade Authority courier and a silent orbital clue, each step tightening the graph of falsified routes, buried logs, and one navigator whose small compromises finally drew a hunter into his shadow.
zh: 它必须终结在一座靠枯竭岩石与旧战争幽灵为生的城市的边缘——在那里，航道在尘土上方低低收窄，每一个进出向量都穿过同一片狭窄天空。在这里，没有人群可以混入，没有风暴走廊可以骑行；唯一的掩护是赛多尼亚伤痕累累郊外腾起的热浪，以及"向量"调过太多次的过载交通信标的静电低语。他选中这地方，是因为它的模式熟悉，是因为十几处小小的航线编辑与安静人情已慢慢编成一条他以为只有自己能看见的逃生线。在这里打断那条线，就能阻止他在公司清理人或绝望走私者把他的把戏变成远更糟的东西之前，把地图折向自己的最后尝试。目前为止，线索从一穷乡星上一块被遗忘的数据板，穿过一艘漂移的贸易管理局信使船与一处沉默的轨道线索，每一步都收紧着那张由伪造航线、被埋日志，以及一名"其小小妥协最终把猎人引向自己阴影"的领航员构成的图。
